messages:
From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>

Cc: security@acme.com
Date: 2026-07-20T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: pen-test artifacts + scope clarification for Acme onboarding

Hi Rishi / Marissa,

As part of our onboarding security review, our InfoSec team needs the following to complete the SIG/SOC-2 evidence pack: 1) a copy or redacted version of your most recent penetration test report, 2) a clear description of what environments that test covered (Hosted API, Dedicated pools, Private/VPC deploys, on-prem packages), and 3) a current remediation status for any high/critical findings.

Specifically: does your pen-test cover Dedicated customers (dedicated GPU pools) the same way it covers the shared Hosted API? For Private/VPC deployments, do you run pen-tests against the customer-managed network, or only provide the test artifacts for the Redwood control plane components?

We can accept a redacted report if needed. Please let us know what you can share and any NDA or access steps required.

Thanks,
Alice Johnson
Security Program Manager — Acme Corporation
[Attachment: SIG-questionnaire.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-07-20T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: pen-test artifacts + scope clarification for Acme onboarding

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear ask, happy to clarify. High-level summary below; I can share a redacted PDF and the current remediation plan once my engineering team signs off.

What our current pen-test covers (most recent engagement, May 2026):
- Hosted API: full coverage (public API endpoints, control plane services, authentication flows, and the Redwood-managed data plane).
- Dedicated: included. Dedicated pools are logical isolation on our hosted platform — the test covered the Dedicated control plane and the dedicated worker pools that run customer workloads (network isolation and tenant separation checks were part of scope).
- Private / VPC: NOT covered by our hosted pen-test for the customer-managed network. For Private/VPC customers we test the Redwood control plane components we manage (agent installer, control APIs, management plane), and we provide customers with guidance and an attestable install checklist. If the customer requests, we can run on-site or managed pen-testing of the Private deployment under a separate engagement (usually requires access and a statement of work).
- On-prem (air-gapped packages): we ship the deployment artifacts and run internal code reviews and a focused build-time security assessment, but on-prem network attack surface testing is performed via customer-led or joint-engagement testing.

Sharing: we can provide a redacted pen-test report that covers Hosted + Dedicated as a single artifact. For Private/VPC or on-prem, we supply the pen-test summary for control plane components and the installation hardening guide; full environment testing is typically provided as a separate engagement.

Next steps: I'll coordinate with Dev and Security (cc'd) to produce a redacted PDF and a remediation spreadsheet. Do you have any specific redaction requirements (IP, exploit PoCs, or internal hostnames)?

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none yet]

Rishi / Marissa — quick update from engineering after triage of May 2026 test artifacts: 

- High/critical findings: 3 total (IDs: PT-2026-041, PT-2026-079, PT-2026-121). All three have been addressed in production with mitigations deployed.
  - PT-2026-041 (auth token rotation weakness): fixed; rotation enforced and tokens invalidated (deployed 2026-06-02).
  - PT-2026-079 (exposed S3 ACL): bucket policy corrected and ACLs removed; audit logs show no data exfiltration (deployed 2026-06-10).
  - PT-2026-121 (worker isolation edge case): patch merged; additional KV cache hardening added (deployed 2026-07-03).

- Medium findings: 7 items; most scheduled in the next two sprints, ETA 2026-08-14 for remaining non-critical items.

- Redaction: we can produce a redacted PDF that strips PoC details, internal hostnames, and stack traces. Attached are the remediation notes and a text file with commit ids for the fixes. Please confirm compliance/Legal sign-off for sharing.

Attachments: [remediation_notes_dev_patel_2026.md (text)], [patch-commit-ids.txt (text)]

Let me know if you want a short tech-brief call with the Acme security engineers — I can do a 30-min walkthrough next week.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Senior Site Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference
